Least width of the dropdown menu panel, which grows from it to fit its longest item on one line. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Greatest width of the dropdown menu panel: past it a long item's words wrap inside the panel. Not in Figma, which draws the panel at one width.
Width of the command palette. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the search field in the wide app bar. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of Figma's phone frames, used for the narrow previews of components that reflow. Not a viewport step; the steps in the size foundation are the layout breakpoints.
Width of the table of contents card. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it.
Width of the popover panel. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the control in a side-by-side field, the label taking the rest of the row. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

Width of the note beside, under or at the end of a button: beside it, the note stays there while this much room is left after the button and moves under it otherwise. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

Least width of the date field beside the time field in a date and time picker; with less room the time field moves under it. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

Height of a line or bar chart's plot, the grid lines and the marks between its value labels. A fixed frame height in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.

Greatest width of the color area, which is square and fills the width it is given up to this. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
Width of the color picker panel. A fixed frame width in Figma with no variable behind it; it should become one.
The viewport width at and above which the text size context switches from min to max. Aliases an existing viewport step rather than introducing a new measurement.

The viewport width at and above which the page counts as wide for layout. Below it, components that reflow for narrow spaces take their narrow form. Aliases the same viewport step as the text-size switch, so the two change together.

The viewport width at and above which a documentation page has room for a column on each side of its content: the sidebar on one side, the table of contents on the other. Aliases an existing viewport step rather than introducing a new measurement.

Diverging scale, far low end. Light orange/700, dark orange/300. Marks reach 3:1 on the plot background; never colour alone: direct labels, markers or patterns too.
Diverging scale, low. Light orange/500, dark orange/500. Marks reach 3:1 on the plot background; never colour alone: direct labels, markers or patterns too.
Diverging scale, the neutral middle (3:1 on both themes). Light grey/500, dark grey/500. Marks reach 3:1 on the plot background; never colour alone: direct labels, markers or patterns too.
Diverging scale, high. Light blue/500, dark blue/500. Marks reach 3:1 on the plot background; never colour alone: direct labels, markers or patterns too.
Diverging scale, far high end. Light blue/700, dark blue/300. Marks reach 3:1 on the plot background; never colour alone: direct labels, markers or patterns too.

Code: numbers, CSS lengths and colors, and true, false and null. Light green/600, dark green/300. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.

Code: function names, CSS functions such as var(), and the command a shell line runs. Light yellow/600, dark yellow/300. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.
Code: type, class and component names. Light teal/600, dark teal/400. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.

Code: keys and properties, such as object and JSON keys, CSS properties and custom properties, HTML and JSX attributes, and command flags. Light blue/800, dark blue/300. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.
Code: comments, the quietest part of the code. Light grey/600, dark grey/400. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.
Code: brackets, commas, colons and operators. Light grey/700, dark grey/300. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.

Code: words that declare or name, such as const, let, function, class, interface, type, new and this. Light blue/600, dark blue/400. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.
Code: HTML and JSX tags, and CSS selectors. Light blue/600, dark blue/400. Text: 4.5:1 or more on the code block's well, in both themes; color is never the only sign of what a piece of code is.

Rhythm of page sections, the largest: the space above and below a hero or a landing section. Compact density shrinks it.

Height of the extra-small control: 24 in both densities, the smallest target allowed. Dashboard recipe: use compact density; 40 for the page’s one main action and for forms; 32 for toolbars and filters, the size used most; 28 for actions inside table rows and cards. On phones switch to comfortable density, or give small controls an invisible 44 px tap area (size/target/comfortable).

Height of a small control: 32 comfortable, 28 compact. Dashboard recipe: use compact density; 40 for the page’s one main action and for forms; 32 for toolbars and filters, the size used most; 28 for actions inside table rows and cards. On phones switch to comfortable density, or give small controls an invisible 44 px tap area (size/target/comfortable).

Height of a medium control, where controls insert by default: 40 comfortable, 32 compact. Dashboard recipe: use compact density; 40 for the page’s one main action and for forms; 32 for toolbars and filters, the size used most; 28 for actions inside table rows and cards. On phones switch to comfortable density, or give small controls an invisible 44 px tap area (size/target/comfortable).

Height of a large control: 48 comfortable, 40 compact. A page may use it for its main call to action; apps use md. A section’s outer side padding: the strip of page between the screen edge and the section’s band. There is no page gutter: the page frame has no padding, and every section, the header and the footer carry this on their own sides. 8 on a phone, 12 on a desktop (comfortable). Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
Space above and below a page section, xs. Phones get less: 16 | 24 (phone | desktop).
Space above and below a page section, sm. Phones get less: 32 | 48 (phone | desktop).
Space above and below a page section, md. Phones get less: 64 | 96 (phone | desktop).
Space above and below a page section, lg. Phones get less: 64 | 128 (phone | desktop).

The sides inside a section’s band, from its edge to its content: 16 on a phone, 32 on a desktop (comfortable). It comes on top of space/layout/gutter, which sits outside the band. Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
From a section heading to its content: 40 on a phone, 56 on a desktop (comfortable). Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
Between blocks and grid items: 32 (comfortable). Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
Beside a split: 32 on a phone, 48 on a desktop (comfortable). Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
Padding inside a raised panel that holds a section: a hero card, a feature block, a call-to-action box. Smaller on phones.
The space between the columns of the page grid, and between cards laid out on it.
A heading to its first paragraph or list: 12 on phones, 16 on wide screens.
A title to the small grey line under it: 4 on phones, 8 on wide screens.
The end of one block of text to the next heading: 24 on phones, 32 on wide screens.
Between two paragraphs (16). Text is not trimmed, so each line’s own leading adds to it.
Between the items of a list (8).
Between a label or title and the line of supporting text right under it, inside a component. None: untrimmed line height already spaces the two lines.
The sticky header’s height, for scroll padding so a focused item is never hidden under it: 56 on a phone, 80 on a desktop. Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
The narrowest grid column, small: 240. Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
The narrowest grid column, medium: 320. Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
The narrowest grid column, large: 400. Each value points to a density token, so compact density still applies.
